title: CORE-7133 · Google review logo oversized fallback src — markup-only, zero pixel change
body:
**Linear:** [CORE-7133](https://linear.app/bsq-group/issue/CORE-7133) · **PR** #118

The filed symptom is **real in the markup but does not reproduce at runtime.** All three open hypotheses
settled empirically on `/director-appointment-resignation`.

## H1 — which candidate is actually fetched

| | DPR 1 | DPR 2 |
|---|---|---|
| live | `1x` 400x135 webp, 9,710 B | `2x` 800x270, 20,190 B |
| clone | `w=256` 256x87 avif, 9,547 B | `w=640` 640x216, 22,207 B |

Both sane at both DPRs. No resolution defect: effective DPR 1.74 at DPR 1, 4.32 at DPR 2.

## H2 — is the `w=3840` fallback ever fetched? **No**

Zero requests for it across four instrumented runs (before/after x DPR 1/2). Chrome ignores `src`
entirely when `srcset` + `sizes` are present.

## H3 — `object-contain` vs `cover`? **The earlier note was wrong**

Live's computed `object-fit` is **`contain`**, not `cover` — both sides letterbox identically into
200x50. Painted logo: live 148.15x50 vs clone 147.13x50 at DPR 1 (1.02px, from the optimiser rounding
86.5 -> 87), and an **exact** match at DPR 2. `object-contain` left alone.

Clone master is **2000x676, identical to live's** — not a wrong-variant media task. No MongoDB write.

## What is actually wrong

`size="200px"` has no `vw` unit, so Next's `getWidths()` returns `{ widths: allSizes, kind: 'w' }` and
`generateImgAttrs()` sets `src` to the largest candidate — `w=3840`, served as the untouched 2000x676
master (30,192 B). Only Google is affected; every other logo has a small master (Trustpilot's `w=3840`
returns 1,880 B).

Fault: `ReviewStatCard/index.tsx:46`, enabled by `Media/ImageMedia/index.tsx:50` having no way to accept
a render width.

## The fix, and its honest value

3 files, ~10 lines, purely additive: `ImageMedia` accepts `width`/`height` and omits `sizes` when given
one; `ReviewStatCard` passes `width={200} height={68}`. That moves it onto the `x`-descriptor path
(`256 1x, 640 2x`), matching live's shape. `width`/`height` did not exist on `Props` before, so
TypeScript guarantees no other call site is affected — `ReviewStatCard` is the only caller.

**After-measurement: zero pixel change.** Logo screenshots byte-identical before vs after at both DPRs
(md5 match; PIL diff 0 differing pixels, empty bbox). Same bytes fetched.
srcset 15 -> 2 entries; `/_next/image` URLs per page 62 -> 36; fallback `src` 2000px -> 640px.

**It is not a payload fix either.** The byte-waste theory assumed the oversized fallback is fetched; it
never is. Image bytes identical. HTML: 246,866 -> 243,744 B raw, but gzip had already collapsed the
near-identical srcset strings — **34,584 -> 34,431 B gzipped = 153 bytes.**

## Disposition

Verified and zero-risk, but buys no pixels and 153 gzipped bytes. Legitimate to merge as markup
correctness, equally legitimate to close as not worth the churn. Should not be prioritised over the
board's real fidelity defects.
acceptanceCriteria: Fallback src is a sane candidate rather than the 2000x676 master.
Zero pixel change — logo renders byte-identically at DPR 1 and DPR 2.
No other ImageMedia call site affected (enforced by the type system).
Decision recorded on whether the markup tidy is worth merging at all.
